newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $63 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $63 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle traded at $63.00 per cwt in light volume, unchanged with this week's sales, feedlot sources said.
About 6,000 head sold in Kansas and light sales may have occured in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area, but none were reported as of mid-afternoon, sources noted.

Fed cattle prices were poised to weaken amid lower beef values and perceptions that next week's Independence Day holiday shortened work schedule would limit packer demand for cattle, several cattle feeders said. Independence Day, July 4, falls on Friday next week.
Beef movement so far this week has outpaced last week's sales, but packers discounted prices heavily to get the job done, some sources said.

Beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.67 to $0.99 per cwt, with 268 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA reported. Choice beef weighing 700-850 lbs was quoted at $101.30, down $0.99 from Wednesday and down $2.49 since prices started falling after last Thursday's close, USDA statistics showed.
Week-to-date fabricated beef sales totalled 1,157 loads as of midday Thursday, up 29.9 percent from 891 sold in the same period last week and up 77 loads from total sales last week.
